dedupe_keys.name: grenfell tower fire and public inquiry london 2017 to 2024

description: The fire at Grenfell Tower, a residential tower block in London, on 14 June 2017 killed 72 people. The public inquiry chaired by Sir Martin Moore-Bick examined it in two phases. The Phase 1 report of 30 October 2019 covered how the fire started, how it escaped the flat of origin and spread through the building, and the emergency response. The Phase 2 report of 4 September 2024, the final report, examined the underlying causes: the design and construction of the cladding system, testing and assurance of construction products, the adequacy of the regulatory regime and the response of central and local government, with 58 recommendations, 37 of them to government. The government's response of 26 February 2025 accepted all findings, reviewed the definition of a higher-risk building with the Building Safety Regulator and began a review of the Approved Documents. Coverage: one building fire with national regulatory consequences in England. Access: reports via the inquiry website, now in the UK Government Web Archive, and GOV.UK. Licence: Crown copyright; OGL for the response. Caveats: the inquiry website could not be read directly here, so facts come from the government response. Simulation uses are fire spread, evacuation and emergency response scenarios for high-rise residential buildings. Related records: the NIST Champlain Towers South investigation.
